# bin: notify: gate agent push notifications by presence/intent

Add a `notify` CLI that decides whether the coding agent's Pushover notifications should fire. **Motivation:** Claude Code sends a push on its Notification/Stop hooks; the author wants them only when away from the laptop, or when explicitly requested — not while pairing with the agent — and the control state should live in the dotfiles, not in `~/.claude`.

Interface (`bin/notify`, on `PATH`):

```bash
notify                 # status: mode, TTL, idle, "would a push fire now?"
notify always [DUR]    # always push (force);  optional auto-expiry
notify never  [DUR]    # never push (silence); optional auto-expiry
notify auto            # default: push only when away (presence-based)
notify run ...         # reserved for #630 (command-timing notifier), not built yet
```

Model: three mutually exclusive modes in one state field (`auto | always | never`), so contradictory combinations cannot exist; `auto` means away if idle ≥ `NOTIFY_AWAY_AFTER` (default 180 s, via `ioreg HIDIdleTime`) or the screensaver is running; `always`/`never` may carry a TTL (`30s|15m|2h|1d`) and fall back to `auto` — the fix for "muted for a call, forgot, missed everything". State: one line `MODE [EXPIRY_EPOCH]` in `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-<DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR>}/agent-notify/mode`, resolved identically and env-independently (via `getconf`) by the CLI and by the hook, cleared on reboot. The hook (`kitchen:agents/scripts/notify-watcher.sh`) reads the same file; the previous `~/.claude/notify.{force,mute}` flags and `afk/back/mute/unmute` aliases are removed. Out of scope: managing the threshold from the CLI, Focus/DND, non-macOS presence, `notify run` ([[DOT-477]]).
